name: Joshua Ertle
bio: Joshua Ertle is an independent candidate for Virginia's 7th Congressional District. He is part of the 'Defending the Unborn' slate of anti-abortion candidates, which runs campaign television advertising across several states.

platform.point: Opposes late-term abortion in Virginia and campaigns against the state's proposed Amendment 1.
Aims to use campaign advertising to show images of aborted fetuses as a strategy to change public opinion.

liberty.evidence: Based on abortion only: opposes late-term abortion and campaigns against Virginia's Amendment 1.

notes: Little public biographical information exists; a candidate directory describes him as a video producer and photographer, which could not be confirmed. The Facebook page 'JoshForVirginia' is assumed to be his campaign page.

name: Randall Terry
bio: Randall Terry founded the anti-abortion group Operation Rescue in 1987 and led it until 1991. He has run for office several times, including as the Constitution Party's 2024 presidential nominee, for the U.S. House in New York and Florida, and for the Florida Senate. He is running as an independent in Virginia's 7th District as part of the 'Defending the Unborn' slate.

platform.point: Seeks to end legal abortion and has said he would also make hormonal birth control illegal.
Uses federal broadcast rules for candidates to air uncensored anti-abortion ads featuring graphic fetal images.

liberty.evidence: Based on abortion and contraception: supports banning abortion and has said birth control pills should be illegal.

notes: No dedicated campaign website was found; he appears on the babies.vote joint fundraising committee site.

name: Don Beyer
bio: Don Beyer has represented Virginia's 8th District in the U.S. House since 2015 and previously chaired the Joint Economic Committee. He was Lieutenant Governor of Virginia from 1990 to 1998 and U.S. Ambassador to Switzerland and Liechtenstein from 2009 to 2013. He owned the Beyer Automotive dealership group and was raised in Washington, D.C.

platform.point: Calls for shutting down ICE, arguing the agency's culture cannot be repaired.
Supports raising taxes on high earners, including restoring a 39.6% top income tax rate.
Backs a tax on carbon pollution and a large expansion of clean electricity.
Supports universal background checks and limits on high-capacity magazines.
Supports keeping and improving the Affordable Care Act.

economy.evidence: Supports restoring the 39.6% top income tax rate and higher estate taxes.

welfare.evidence: Supports defending and expanding the Affordable Care Act and free community college.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights and marijuana reform, while backing gun restrictions such as universal background checks.

immigration.evidence: Supports the DREAM Act and a path to citizenship, and has called for shutting down ICE.

foreign.evidence: Voted to support Israel after October 7 and opposes a nuclear Iran, while requiring congressional approval for military action.

energy.evidence: Supports a carbon tax, 50% clean electricity by 2030 and a ban on offshore drilling.

education.evidence: Opposes school vouchers and supports Education Department funding and free community college.

notes: The earlier faith score of 10 was removed because no clear evidence on religion in public life was found. No campaign website was confirmed.

name: Tony Sabio
current_role: Navy veteran and former CIA officer
bio: Tony Sabio served in the U.S. Navy from 1996 to 2012 and later worked for the Secret Service and the CIA, as well as in the private sector. He was born in San Juan, Puerto Rico, grew up in San Diego and has lived in Virginia since 2002. He won the Republican nomination for Virginia's 8th District unopposed.

platform.point: Proposes an Energy Affordability and American Power Act to expand small modular reactors and make large energy users fund new generation.
Proposes an American Jobs and Opportunity Act to create jobs not dependent on the federal government.
Proposes a Small Business First Act to protect and grow local small businesses.
Proposes a Safe Communities and Secure America Act focused on community safety and national security.
Proposes an American Health Freedom Plan as one of his five campaign pillars.
Says ICE needs more accountability but should not be abolished.

energy.evidence: His energy plan centers on small modular nuclear reactors, grid upgrades and protecting ratepayers from data center power costs.

tech.evidence: Cautioned against fear-driven responses to AI and data centers, saying new technology should not be rejected in advance.

notes: Campaign planks are named bills with little published detail. He describes himself as a Reagan-style conservative guided by his Christian faith and the Constitution.

name: Shelly Arnoldi
bio: Shelly Arnoldi is a Fairfax County resident, U.S. Navy veteran and licensed professional engineer who works as a federal engineer and has been active with Moms for Liberty in Fairfax. She ran for the Virginia House of Delegates in District 16 in 2025. She was born in Sheboygan, Wisconsin, and studied at Marquette University and Old Dominion University.

platform.point: Pledges to cut government waste and bureaucracy.
Opposes government overreach, citing school closures and mask mandates, and seeks support from medical-freedom voters.
Supports parental rights in children's education.
Opposes defunding ICE and supports deporting people in the country illegally, especially those receiving benefits.
Wants data center expansion paused until its impacts are understood.

economy.evidence: Lists free markets, limited government and fiscal responsibility as core principles and pledges to cut waste.

immigration.evidence: Opposes defunding ICE and supports deporting people in the country illegally.

foreign.evidence: Describes her foreign policy as pro-peace and anti-war while maintaining strength.

tech.evidence: Called for halting data center expansion until impacts are understood, though she distrusts government oversight.

education.evidence: Says she entered politics over school closures and the erosion of parental rights, and campaigns on parental rights.

notes: Her campaign site lists broad principles rather than detailed policies; positions come mainly from local news coverage. Liberty was left unscored because she described abortion and term limits as voter concerns rather than stating her own positions.

name: Tim Sharman
bio: Tim Sharman is an independent candidate for Virginia's 8th District. Born in London, he studied politics, philosophy and economics at Oxford, moved to the United States about 30 years ago and became a citizen. He worked helping companies serve customers and founded a customer-experience startup.

platform.point: Prioritizes lowering costs of housing, childcare, health care, education, groceries and transportation.
Proposes an 'Affordable Healthcare Moonshot' to reduce health care costs.
Proposes an American Opportunity Fund Act as part of an economy-of-opportunity agenda.
Says ICE should be fundamentally restructured rather than eliminated.
Prefers local decisions over federal mandates on regulating data centers.

notes: Detailed issue pages could not be retrieved, so no position scores were assigned.

name: Morgan Griffith
bio: Morgan Griffith has represented Virginia's 9th District in the U.S. House since 2011. He served in the Virginia House of Delegates from 1994 to 2011, including as Majority Leader from 2000 to 2010. Before Congress he practiced law in the Roanoke and Salem area, where he grew up.

platform.point: Opposes tax increases and signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge.
Opposes EPA rules on coal mining and backs an all-of-the-above energy strategy.
Favors market-based health care reforms over expanding the Affordable Care Act.
Introduced legislation to move marijuana to Schedule II to allow medical use under federal law.
Supports banning abortion after 20 weeks except to save the mother's life, and opposes federal abortion funding.

economy.evidence: Signed the no-new-taxes pledge and supported cutting the corporate tax rate to 21%.

welfare.evidence: Opposes expanding the Affordable Care Act and favors market-based reforms.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion after 20 weeks, while opposing gun restrictions and backing medical marijuana rescheduling.

security.evidence: Voted to extend PATRIOT Act roving wiretaps and supports cybersecurity data-sharing with government.

immigration.evidence: Opposes amnesty and voted to bar DREAMers from military service.

foreign.evidence: Supported moving the U.S. embassy to Jerusalem and authorized military action against Iran if needed.

energy.evidence: Opposes EPA coal rules, supports offshore drilling and signed the No Climate Tax Pledge.

education.evidence: Mixed record: supports D.C. opportunity scholarships but is listed as opposing broader private school vouchers.

faith.evidence: OnTheIssues rates his voting record as neutral on keeping religion in the public sphere.

notes: Faith score changed from 70 to 50 because OnTheIssues rates his record as neutral on religion in public life. Much of the OnTheIssues evidence reflects older votes.

name: Joy Powers
bio: Joy Powers is a farmer and small-business owner running for Congress in Virginia's 9th District. She is a public school graduate and describes herself as an advocate for public education.

platform.point: Go after price gouging and corporate consolidation in food, seed and medicine, and ease tariff costs on farmers and families.
Would protect federal Medicaid funding to prevent rural hospital closures and service cuts.
Supports farm bills that help family-scale producers with safety nets and right-to-repair rules.
Opposes large data centers receiving tax breaks that raise power costs and strain water supplies.
Supports strong public school funding, fair teacher pay and career and technical education.
Opposes unconditional military aid to Israel and foreign lobby influence on U.S. policy.

economy.evidence: Wants to go after price gouging and corporate consolidation and says tariffs have raised costs.

welfare.evidence: Would protect federal Medicaid funding and invest in childcare and broadband for rural areas.

liberty.evidence: Supports Second Amendment rights for gun owners and equal legal protection for LGBTQ Virginians.

foreign.evidence: Opposes unconditional military aid to Israel.

energy.evidence: Opposes tax-break-backed data centers that raise power costs and drain water resources.

education.evidence: Supports strong public school funding and fair teacher pay.

notes: Liberty score is based on guns and LGBTQ rights only; no abortion position was found on her priorities page.

name: Suhas Subramanyam
bio: Suhas Subramanyam has represented Virginia's 10th District in the U.S. House since January 2025. He previously served in the Virginia Senate (2024-2025) and the Virginia House of Delegates (2020-2024). He was a White House technology policy adviser under President Obama and a technology lawyer, and was born in Houston, Texas.

platform.point: Wants lower drug prices through Medicare negotiation, price transparency and expanded mental health services.
Supports abortion rights and IVF access, and sponsored a state constitutional amendment on reproductive freedom.
Supports gun violence prevention laws while respecting the Second Amendment.
Treats climate change as an emergency and backs renewable energy and conservation.
Supports AI rules that protect consumers while allowing innovation, and clear rules for blockchain.
Focuses on small business growth, protecting federal jobs and lowering costs.

economy.evidence: Supports Medicare drug price negotiation and pushed utility overcharge refunds for ratepayers.

welfare.evidence: Advocates expanded health care access and mental health services with lower costs.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights and IVF access, while backing gun violence prevention laws.

immigration.evidence: Voted for the Laken Riley Act on detaining migrants charged with crimes.

energy.evidence: Calls climate change an emergency requiring immediate action and renewable energy.

tech.evidence: Supports AI regulation to protect consumers while allowing growth.

name: Dave Beckwith
bio: Dave Beckwith served 30 years in the U.S. Air Force, retiring as a colonel, and was a Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense. He has lived in Loudoun County for 17 years and homeschools his children.

platform.point: Supports lower taxes, fewer regulations and an all-of-the-above energy strategy to cut costs.
Wants balanced budgets and less wasteful spending and fraud.
Supports well-resourced law enforcement agencies.
Backs market-based energy solutions including renewed investment in nuclear power.
Emphasizes parental rights, vocational training and more apprenticeships.
Prioritizes timely health care, mental health services and earned benefits for veterans.

economy.evidence: Supports lower taxes, reduced regulation and balanced budgets.

welfare.evidence: Wants affordable health care without government overreach and less wasteful spending.

security.evidence: Describes himself as a strong supporter of well-resourced law enforcement.

energy.evidence: Backs an all-of-the-above, market-based energy strategy including nuclear power.

notes: His campaign also lists a Facebook page, but no URL was confirmed.

name: Ahsen Malik
bio: Ahsen Malik is an independent candidate for Virginia's 10th Congressional District. His name appears on the ballot as Ahsen Mujeeb Malik.
notes: Local coverage reports no visible campaign presence, and no website, social accounts or policy statements were found.

name: James Walkinshaw
bio: James Walkinshaw has represented Virginia's 11th District in the U.S. House since September 2025. He served on the Fairfax County Board of Supervisors for the Braddock District from 2020 to 2025 and was chief of staff to Rep. Gerry Connolly from 2009 to 2019. He was born in Arlington and grew up in Prince William County.

platform.point: Advocates protections and pay increases for federal employees.
Pledges to oppose Trump administration policies and strengthen congressional oversight.
Opposes current tariff policies and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
Opposes current deportation policies and supports comprehensive reform with a path to citizenship.
Lists improving cybersecurity and supporting small businesses among his priorities.

economy.evidence: Opposes current tariffs and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

welfare.evidence: Opposes the health care cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights and backed a gun ban in Fairfax County buildings.

immigration.evidence: Opposes current deportation policies and supports a path to citizenship.

foreign.evidence: Supports aid to Ukraine and views Israel as a key ally while calling for a Gaza ceasefire.

energy.evidence: Supported moving the Fairfax County fleet to electric vehicles as a supervisor.

tech.evidence: Has called for oversight of AI and prioritizes cybersecurity.

education.evidence: Opposes dismantling the Department of Education.

notes: Energy, tech and gun-ban evidence carries over from earlier research and was not re-verified in this pass.
